title: anchored-cfg-fallback-token-frag-reconstruction-and-streaming-fragment-reassembler
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Add anchored-grammar fallback and streaming fragment reassembly to reduce constrained-decoding failures on token-boundary splits. Backwards compatible; opt-in via config. Improves stability for long-streaming schema/toolcall workloads.
description:
Motivation: Constrained decoding using CFG/grammar backends repeatedly failed in streaming scenarios where tokenizers split grammar anchors across chunk boundaries. This surfaced as hard-to-debug 'no valid production' errors or truncated structured outputs for tool/function-calling flows. Existing fallback rules were either too aggressive (fall back to greedy sampling) or too permissive (allow invalid tokens).

What this PR does: Implements an anchored-grammar fallback strategy combined with a streaming fragment reassembler that: 1) detects when grammar anchors (literal tokens, opening braces, tool-call delimiters) are split across streaming chunk boundaries; 2) reassembles token fragments using the tokenizer's byte-level API and a small windowed buffer before invoking the CFG matcher; 3) if reconstruction fails within the buffer window, falls back to a deterministic regex-sampling backend that enforces anchor presence without permitting arbitrary tokens; 4) emits detailed telemetry and a new metric (constrained.fragment_reassembly.{attempts,succeeds,fails}) to tune buffer sizes.

Compatibility and opt-in: The feature is off by default for Dedicated/Private customers and enabled by default on hosted for 30% of traffic as a canary. Runtime is configurable via decoder.config: {"anchored_fragment_reassembly": {"enabled": true|false, "max_buffer_bytes": 48, "regex_fallback_threshold": 0.65}}. The decoder falls back to existing behavior when the tokenizer does not expose byte-level boundaries.

Implementation notes: - Added streaming buffer + fragment index in the runtime that ties to request IDs and cleans up on completion/timeouts. - Introduced an AnchorScanner that conservatively identifies anchor tokens in grammar ASTs and marks them as "fragile". - Reuse tokenizer's encode/offset map to attempt reassembly: we accept a maximum of 48 bytes of lookback; larger fragments trigger regex fallback to avoid unbounded memory. - Regex fallback implements a prioritized, deterministic sampler that only emits tokens that keep the anchor intact; it's deliberately narrower than full CFG to preserve semantics when reassembly fails. - Added conservative CPU path and a fast GPU-compatible path: GPU path avoids re-encoding where possible by consulting cached token edges.

Testing and CI: - Unit: new tests for splitter/reassembler, AnchorScanner edge cases, regex fallback determinism (added 23 unit tests). - Integration: end-to-end streaming test harness that simulates 1k fragmented streams across 12 grammars (passes). - Perf: microbenchmarks show a median inference overhead of +0.7% at max_buffer_bytes=48, 95th percentile +1.6% under high concurrency. - Canary: 30% hosted rollout with monitoring dashboards and auto-roll-back runbook.

Related: Addresses regressions surfaced by SUP-9987 and complements ENG-1283 (grammar robustness work). Does not replace larger constrained-solver redesign in ENG-1400.

Checklist: - [x] Implement AnchorScanner and reassembly buffer - [x] Add deterministic regex fallback sampler - [x] Add telemetry and dashboards - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Canary rollout config and docs snippets

Operational notes: - Consumers using custom grammars that embed binary blobs may see false positives; recommend setting max_buffer_bytes to 0 in those cases. - Metric alerts should be added for fragment_reassembly.fails > 0.5% over 1h during canary.

Rollout plan: Merge -> Canary 30% hosted (3 days) -> Evaluate metrics and error rates -> Ramp to 100% hosted -> Optionally enable default for Dedicated after feedback.

Contributors: Priya N. (author) + Diego A. (regex sampler), with reviews from Liam and Maya.

reviews: Liam O'Connor: LGTM overall. A few nits on locking in stream_fragment_buffer (race on request cleanup). Please add a stress test that forces tokenizers with variable byte-length encodings.
Priya Natarajan: Addressed locking nit; added a stress test harness that runs mixed UTF-8/UTF-16 surrogate pairs and added a cleanup TTL of 5s. PTAL.

Maya Chen: Commented on regex fallback threshold semantics. Suggest making threshold 0.5 by default and moving the param into 'preserved_anchors' tuning group. Also requested a small doc blurb about Dedicated opt-in.
Priya Natarajan: Lowered default threshold to 0.5 and added Dedicated opt-in notes to docs. Responded to all comments.
Diego Alvarez: Approving after verifying deterministic outputs on sampled grammars and confirming metrics emitted as expected.
